summary: The RLS policy uses `using (true)`, so any authenticated user can read every row in public.invoices. Restrict it to the owner, e.g. `using (auth.uid() = user_id)`.
User-controlled `q` and `sort` are interpolated directly into SQL via $queryRawUnsafe, allowing SQL injection. Use parameterized queries and an allowlist for the sort column.

The email input has only a placeholder and no accessible label, so screen-reader users get no persistent name for the field. Add an associated <label> (or aria-label) and type="email"/autocomplete="email".

The payment amount and currency are taken directly from the client request body, so a user can pay any amount they choose. Compute the amount server-side from trusted product/cart data and authenticate the request.
The search term is parameterized with LIKE wildcards escaped, and sort is restricted to an allowlist of Prisma.sql fragments; no security problem found.
A Supabase service_role JWT is embedded in frontend code, giving anyone full database access that bypasses RLS. Remove it, rotate the key immediately, and use the anon/publishable key in the client.

Open, confirmed high-severity finding AG-001 on the release commit shows any signed-in user can read another user's invoice (runtime test failed with 200 instead of 404); green unit tests do not override this. Release is blocked until it is fixed and re-verified.

saveNote retries immediately without backoff, sends no Content-Type, and silently returns on final failure, so the caller believes the note was saved when it was lost; retrying a non-idempotent POST can also create duplicates. Surface the failure, add backoff, and use an idempotency key.

The tool reads all invoices through an admin database client with no user scoping or authorization, exposing every customer's invoices to whoever invokes it. Scope the query to the authenticated user and use a non-privileged client.
Only a Supabase publishable key is exposed, which is intended for client use; no problem found.
The route requires an authenticated user and returns 404 unless the invoice belongs to that user; no problem found.
The invoice route has no authentication or ownership check, so anyone can fetch any invoice by ID (IDOR). Require the user and return 404 unless invoice.userId matches.
README typo fix only; no security, privacy, reliability, or accessibility impact.

Coupon redemption is a check-then-update race, so concurrent requests can redeem the same single-use coupon more than once. Use an atomic conditional update (where code and redeemed=false) or a transaction and check the affected row count.

Premium is unlocked just by rendering the success page, without verifying the payment server-side, so anyone can visit the page to get premium for free. Grant entitlements only from a verified payment webhook or server-side payment check.
The RLS policy restricts authenticated users to invoices where auth.uid() = user_id; no problem found.

The audit has an open critical finding (service-role credential in client code) and the critical 'secrets' mandatory check FAILs, which contradicts the summary's GO; the finding's commit also does not match the audited head. Record NO-GO until the key is removed and rotated and the check passes.

Static reading shows the route requires a user and returns 404 when the invoice is not theirs, but with no database, test run, or staging URL the ownership check could not be executed, so it is recorded as not tested.
